notes: Guardian-and-ward dispute over authority to lease ward's commercial store buildings and subletting rights; no lodging/boarding-house occupancy involved.
Ordinary landlord-tenant rent dispute over a house leased by church trustees to tenants; no lodger/boarder or regulatory issue present.
Facts recite a rooming house being leased/subleased with furniture, but the adjudicated issue is conversion of chattels and limitations, not the legal character of the letting.

Nuisance-abatement statute lists 'hotel, rooming house or boarding house' as one category of premises subject to closure for liquor/gambling/prostitution, but the actual premises is a social club and the holding is purely procedural (ex parte closure order improper).
Railway station premises-liability case regarding duty owed to a licensee bidding a passenger farewell; no dwelling/lodging occupancy issue.
Gambling-control prosecution; defendant's operation of the second story as a 'rooming house' is mentioned only to establish control of premises over an attic used for gaming.
Injunction case concerning bawdyhouses/disorderly houses and a municipal ordinance confining them to a district; does not involve boarding/lodging houses or compensated room-letting.
Partnership/adverse-possession dispute over an employee's occupancy of a firm-owned house as part of employment consideration; not a compensated lodging arrangement.
Tenancy-in-common land partition dispute; no dwelling/lodging occupancy issue.
Agricultural cropper/landlord-tenant classification dispute over a farm rental; incidental mention of the cropper living in one room does not implicate the lodging/boarding doctrine.

holding_summary: In a libel suit by a man who ran a rooming house in his own home near the Union Station, the court held the petition insufficient because the libelous article referred to a 'bunch of whorehouses ... placarded as "Rooming Houses"' and no facts were pled connecting plaintiff's single rooming house to that class. The court refused to infer, from the mere fact that a house is placarded as offering furnished rooms for rent, that it is therefore a whorehouse.

quotes.text: such rooms in the house as were not occupied for family purposes by plaintiff and his father and mother were held out to the traveling public and the public in general for rent, and were on divers occasions rented to other persons

It may be conceded that a whorehouse may be so placarded as to appear to be a rooming house, but we cannot agree to the converse of the proposition which plaintiff seems to urge in his petition, without sufficient averments of fact to sustain his conclusion that a rooming house, or a house with furnished rooms for rent, and so placarded, may reasonably be considered to be a whorehouse by reason of its placards.
No allegation by way of colloquium was made to show that plaintiff’s house was included in the class denominated “whorehouses.”

notes: Householder rented rooms not needed for family use to the traveling public at nightly/daily rates; court treats such a legitimate furnished-rooms business as distinct from a disorderly house.
Fire-insurance occupancy-warranty dispute over a sanitarium building; not a lodging/boarding-house occupancy case.

quotes.text: the tenant reconvened for damages from being compelled to abandon the premises, preventing her from keeping boarders therein
the profits alleged and attempted to be proven were too vague, uncertain, and speculative to be recoverable in an action at law.

notes: Tenant's boarding-house business is treated as an ordinary commercial tenancy (favorable), but her damages claim tied to it was rejected under general speculative-profits doctrine, not on grounds specific to boarding-house legality (adverse-leaning); no clear lease/license/lodging characterization of the boarder relationship is stated, so characterization left null.
Concerns whether a private country club's dispensing of liquor to members constitutes 'selling' under tax/injunction statutes; no lodging or boarding-house issue.

Suit is a landlord-tenant dispute over rent and lease extension of a lodging-house building among successive operators; the legal character of the operator's letting to roomers/lodgers is never adjudicated.
Dispute over rent under a land lease and the mental competency of the lessor at the time of a deed; no dwelling/lodging occupancy issue.
Farm-land rent dispute between a life tenant and her tenant; no dwelling/lodging occupancy issue.

quotes.text: Mrs. Dubose testified that appellant came to her house in Uvalde about the 12th of September and she let him have two furnished rooms in which he and his wife and child lived until the 23d of October, when they moved to Mrs. Greaves where they resided at the time of the trial. They did their own cooking and ate in the rooms and slept there.

if you believe from the evidence that J. Less was an actual dweller in Uvalde County, Texas, at the time that he practiced medicine, if he did so, and that he had removed from some other place, and brought his wife and child with him, and was keeping house with such wife and child in said Uvalde County, Texas, and had come to Uvalde County, Texas, for the purpose of remaining some time, and practicing medicine (if he did so intend) . . . then and in that case he would be residing in Uvalde County, Texas, within the purview of said law.

notes: A householder's short-term letting of furnished rooms to a family is treated as an unremarkable, lawful basis for establishing actual residence; the letting arrangement itself is never questioned.
